findings.title: Field injection with @Autowired is used in test code
findings.description: The zero-tolerance checklist prohibits @Autowired field injection anywhere in the target. GreetingControllerTest injects MockMvc into a mutable field instead of using constructor injection.
findings.evidence:
@Autowired
private MockMvc mockMvc;
findings.suggestedFix: Use JUnit 5 constructor injection: `GreetingControllerTest(MockMvc mockMvc) { this.mockMvc = mockMvc; }` with a `private final MockMvc mockMvc;` field.

findings.title: Spring Service is directly instantiated with new
findings.description: The zero-tolerance checklist prohibits direct instantiation of DI-target Service classes. GreetingServiceTest creates `new GreetingService()` directly instead of obtaining the service through Spring or isolating the pure logic outside a Spring-managed Service.

findings.title: Some invalid requests can bypass the unified ErrorResponse shape
findings.description: GlobalExceptionHandler centralizes several validation exceptions, but the GET endpoint has a required `name` query parameter. If the parameter is omitted, Spring MVC raises MissingServletRequestParameterException, which is not handled here and can fall back to Spring Boot's default error body instead of the project's ErrorResponse contract.
findings.evidence: Handlers exist for MethodArgumentNotValidException, HandlerMethodValidationException, and ConstraintViolationException only; GreetingController requires `@RequestParam ... String name` at line 47.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an `@ExceptionHandler(MissingServletRequestParameterException.class)` that returns the same sanitized `ErrorResponse`, and add a MockMvc test for `/api/greetings` without `name`.

findings.title: Service layer depends on API/presentation DTO

findings.category: A01 Broken Access Control / Security Baseline
findings.title: No Spring Security configuration or default-deny authorization boundary
findings.description: The application exposes /api/health and /api/greetings endpoints but has no spring-boot-starter-security dependency and no SecurityFilterChain. This means there is no default-deny authorization boundary, no framework CSRF integration, and no Spring Security header hardening. The current sample endpoints do not expose sensitive records, so the immediate data-exposure impact is limited, but this is unsafe as a reusable OSS Spring Boot baseline.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include validation, web, and test starters only; no spring-boot-starter-security. Controller mappings are present at sample-java-code/src/main/java/com/codexskishop/sample/api/GreetingController.java:20,34,45,57.
findings.suggestedFix: Add spring-boot-starter-security and a SecurityFilterChain. Explicitly permit only intended public endpoints such as /api/health, require authentication or a documented public contract for others, and keep anyRequest().authenticated() as the fallback.

findings.title: Security headers are not configured
findings.description: No configuration was found for Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or Server header suppression. Even JSON APIs benefit from these browser-facing controls, especially once endpoints are consumed by a frontend or exposed publicly.
findings.evidence: application.yml only sets server.port and spring.application.name. Targeted search found no SecurityFilterChain or header configuration in sample-java-code.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure headers through Spring Security, for example contentTypeOptions, frameOptions deny, CSP default-src 'self', HSTS for HTTPS deployments, strict-origin-when-cross-origin referrer policy, camera/microphone/geolocation permissions policy, and set server.server-header to blank where supported.

findings.title: POST endpoint has no CSRF protection or documented stateless API policy
findings.description: POST /api/greetings is exposed without Spring Security, so CSRF protection is unavailable. The current operation appears stateless and low impact, but the codebase does not document or enforce an API-only stateless policy. If this pattern is copied to state-changing endpoints, cross-site request submission becomes exploitable.
findings.evidence: @PostMapping("/greetings") accepts a JSON request body. pom.xml has no Spring Security dependency and targeted search found no csrf configuration.
findings.suggestedFix: If browser session authentication will be used, enable Spring Security CSRF with CookieCsrfTokenRepository and require tokens on state-changing requests. If this is intentionally a stateless public API, document that decision and require non-cookie authentication before adding state-changing endpoints.

findings.category: D Denial of Service / Rate Limiting
findings.title: Public endpoints have no rate limiting
findings.description: The health and greeting endpoints are public and no rate limiting filter, gateway policy, or bucket implementation was found. An attacker can flood /api/health or /api/greetings to consume request threads and application resources. This is especially relevant because these endpoints are intended for smoke or command checks and may be exposed in CI/demo environments.
findings.evidence: Public endpoint mappings exist for GET /api/health, GET /api/greetings, and POST /api/greetings. Targeted search found no Bucket4j, rate limiter, OncePerRequestFilter, FilterRegistrationBean, or gateway rate-limit configuration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a small rate-limiting filter or gateway policy for public endpoints. Use stricter limits for POST endpoints and a separate inexpensive health-check path policy for infrastructure probes.

findings.category: D Denial of Service / Request Limits
findings.title: HTTP request-size and connection timeout limits are not explicitly configured
findings.description: The API accepts query parameters and JSON request bodies, but application.yml does not set servlet/Tomcat request-size or connection timeout limits. findings.suggestedFix: Rename methods, for example should_returnGreetingWithNormalizedWhitespace_when_nameContainsRepeatedWhitespace(), should_throwIllegalArgumentException_when_nameIsBlank(), should_throwIllegalArgumentException_when_nameIsNull().

findings.suggestedFix: Add @DisplayName annotations describing the behavior in natural language, while keeping method names in should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition form.

findings.title: Controller tests collapse Act and Assert into one MockMvc chain
findings.description: The controller tests call mockMvc.perform(...).andExpect(...) as one fluent statement without clear Arrange / Act / Assert separation. The required AAA structure is not visible, and Act is not isolated as a single result-producing call.
findings.evidence: Each test directly chains mockMvc.perform(...) with andExpect(...) assertions.
findings.suggestedFix: Store the action result before assertions, for example: // Act var result = mockMvc.perform(...); // Assert result.andExpect(...); Add blank lines or comments between Arrange, Act, and Assert.

findings.evidence: assertThat(greetingService.greet(...).message()) and assertThatThrownBy(() -> greetingService.greet(...)) combine Act and Assert.

findings.title: Size boundary validation is not tested
findings.description: GreetingController validates name with @Size(max = 40), but tests only cover normal and blank values. Boundary cases at exactly 40 characters and 41 characters are missing.
findings.evidence: Tests cover valid short names and blank names, but no test exercises @Size(max = 40) on query or body inputs.

findings.category: A01 Broken Access Control / Security Baseline
findings.title: No Spring Security configuration or default-deny authorization boundary
findings.description: The application exposes /api/health and /api/greetings endpoints but has no spring-boot-starter-security dependency and no SecurityFilterChain. This means there is no default-deny authorization boundary, no framework CSRF integration, and no Spring Security header hardening. The current sample endpoints do not expose sensitive records, so the immediate data-exposure impact is limited, but this is unsafe as a reusable OSS Spring Boot baseline.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include validation, web, and test starters only; no spring-boot-starter-security. Controller mappings are present at sample-java-code/src/main/java/com/codexskishop/sample/api/GreetingController.java:20,34,45,57.
findings.suggestedFix: Add spring-boot-starter-security and a SecurityFilterChain. Explicitly permit only intended public endpoints such as /api/health, require authentication or a documented public contract for others, and keep anyRequest().authenticated() as the fallback.

findings.title: Security headers are not configured
findings.description: No configuration was found for Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or Server header suppression. Even JSON APIs benefit from these browser-facing controls, especially once endpoints are consumed by a frontend or exposed publicly.
findings.evidence: application.yml only sets server.port and spring.application.name. Targeted search found no SecurityFilterChain or header configuration in sample-java-code.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure headers through Spring Security, for example contentTypeOptions, frameOptions deny, CSP default-src 'self', HSTS for HTTPS deployments, strict-origin-when-cross-origin referrer policy, camera/microphone/geolocation permissions policy, and set server.server-header to blank where supported.

findings.title: POST endpoint has no CSRF protection or documented stateless API policy
findings.description: POST /api/greetings is exposed without Spring Security, so CSRF protection is unavailable. The current operation appears stateless and low impact, but the codebase does not document or enforce an API-only stateless policy. If this pattern is copied to state-changing endpoints, cross-site request submission becomes exploitable.
findings.evidence: @PostMapping("/greetings") accepts a JSON request body. pom.xml has no Spring Security dependency and targeted search found no csrf configuration.
findings.suggestedFix: If browser session authentication will be used, enable Spring Security CSRF with CookieCsrfTokenRepository and require tokens on state-changing requests. If this is intentionally a stateless public API, document that decision and require non-cookie authentication before adding state-changing endpoints.

findings.category: D Denial of Service / Rate Limiting
findings.title: Public endpoints have no rate limiting
findings.description: The health and greeting endpoints are public and no rate limiting filter, gateway policy, or bucket implementation was found. An attacker can flood /api/health or /api/greetings to consume request threads and application resources. This is especially relevant because these endpoints are intended for smoke or command checks and may be exposed in CI/demo environments.
findings.evidence: Public endpoint mappings exist for GET /api/health, GET /api/greetings, and POST /api/greetings. Targeted search found no Bucket4j, rate limiter, OncePerRequestFilter, FilterRegistrationBean, or gateway rate-limit configuration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a small rate-limiting filter or gateway policy for public endpoints. Use stricter limits for POST endpoints and a separate inexpensive health-check path policy for infrastructure probes.

findings.category: D Denial of Service / Request Limits
findings.title: HTTP request-size and connection timeout limits are not explicitly configured
findings.description: The API accepts query parameters and JSON request bodies, but application.yml does not set servlet/Tomcat request-size or connection timeout limits. Field validation limits name to 40 characters after binding, but large bodies are parsed before Bean Validation rejects invalid payloads, leaving a resource-exhaustion path.
findings.evidence: application.yml contains only server.port and spring.application.name. Targeted search found no server.tomcat.max-http-form-post-size, max-swallow-size, connection-timeout, keep-alive-timeout, or servlet multipart limits.
findings.suggestedFix: Set bounded request and connection settings appropriate for the sample, such as server.tomcat.max-http-form-post-size, server.tomcat.connection-timeout, server.tomcat.keep-alive-timeout, and any multipart limits if file upload is later added.

findings.title: Global exception handling covers validation errors only
findings.description: Validation failures are sanitized, which is good, but the global handler does not cover unexpected exceptions or common request parsing failures. Current Spring Boot defaults usually avoid stack traces in responses, but the target does not explicitly set server.error.include-stacktrace/include-message or provide a generic sanitized fallback. Future changes could accidentally leak exception messages or framework error details.
findings.evidence: Handlers exist for MethodArgumentNotValidException, HandlerMethodValidationException, and ConstraintViolationException only. application.yml has no server.error.include-stacktrace or server.error.include-message settings.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit production-safe error properties: server.error.include-stacktrace=never and server.error.include-message=never. Consider a generic @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) that returns a sanitized error with a correlation ID while logging server-side details safely.
